findings.title: #974 AC1's "its own affordance ... each distinct from every other kind's" is not met: the new kind reuses fixed_asset_incomplete / staff_advance_incomplete's destination verbatim
findings.evidence: Ticket line (Acceptance criteria, first box): "A client with a proposed, unsigned authority produces exactly one queue row, with its own label and its own affordance opening to where the authority can be signed or withdrawn, each distinct from every other kind's." On the branch: apps/web/components/firm/needs-you-affordances.tsx:120 registers `depreciation_authority_pending: null` (NO affordance component at all); apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you-links.ts:88-91 maps it to "/registers", the same suffix `fixed_asset_incomplete` and `staff_advance_incomplete` already carry, and apps/web/messages/en.json NeedsYou.openTab gains `"depreciation_authority_pending": "Open the registers tab"`, byte-identical to the other two. The implementer's own new cell concedes it: apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you-links.test.ts:28-30 comments "a proposed depreciation authority is signed or withdrawn on the SAME register tab fixed_asset_incomplete/staff_advance_incomplete already open" and asserts the identical href. Note also that `fixed_asset_incomplete` narrows further (needsYouRowHref -> fixedAssetHref), so the new kind is strictly the least specific of the three. The label alone IS distinct ("Depreciation authority awaiting signature"), so only the affordance half of the AC fails. The ticket report (wave2-lane07-ticket974.md, AC1) cites `p974.row.distinct` as the evidence for this line; re-read, that cell (packages/db/tests/depreciation-authority-pending-rowkind.test.mjs:91-101) only proves two different clients' authority ids do not collide — it says nothing about affordance distinctness, so the AC is asserted rather than evidenced.
findings.required_fix: Either (a) make the affordance distinct — e.g. an inline affordance component for the kind, or a deeper destination/anchor that lands on DepreciationAuthorityPanel rather than the register tab root, with its own NeedsYou.openTab string; or (b) get an owner ruling that the shared register tab satisfies AC1 and record it on #974, then correct the report's cited evidence.

findings.title: #998 AC1 ("No reference to the function or the wrapper remains outside migration history") leaves two references that now point at things this ticket deleted
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "- [ ] No reference to the function or the wrapper remains outside migration history." The ticket's Context does carve out "Two comments in unrelated modules mention it as background", but after the drop those comments name artefacts that no longer exist: apps/web/lib/firm/activity.ts:31-32 still reads "the same reasoning lib/firm/timeline.ts's own header gives for `list_firm_timeline`" — `apps/web/lib/firm/timeline.ts` was DELETED by this ticket (confirmed: `ls apps/web/lib/firm/timeline.ts` -> No such file), so the pointer is dangling; and apps/web/e2e/home-board-mock.mjs:292-293 still documents "`list_firm_timeline` is DELIBERATELY NOT HANDLED. This mock exercises the compatibility arm for a database that predates migration 0174, so Firm Home renders its 'not available yet' state" — an arm #659 already removed and the function no longer exists to predate. Live code is clean (verified by grep over apps/web, packages/runtime, packages/db and by operation-census.test.mjs opcen.1/opcen.3 re-run green), so this is documentation rot introduced by the retirement, not a broken call site.
findings.required_fix: Reword apps/web/lib/firm/activity.ts:31-32 so it no longer points at a deleted file, and reword apps/web/e2e/home-board-mock.mjs:292-296 so it no longer describes a compatibility arm and a door that are both gone.

findings.title: #995 removed Firm Home's only surface for a failed client-register read, which no ticket line asked for
findings.evidence: The brief's Desired behavior is scoped to the summary: "The rendered status tally is removed. The portfolio table is Firm Home's one client-population summary for a bookkeeper or higher. A caller below that floor still sees a plain client count...". Nothing asks for the register-read failure face to go. The retired `<section aria-labelledby="firm-home-clients">` carried the DataState wrapper that rendered "Something went wrong" on `register.error`; with it gone, a failed register read now degrades silently to the header's role-only sentence. The change is visible in the pre-existing cell that had to be rewritten: apps/web/components/firm/firm-home/firm-home-board.test.tsx:327-336, where `assert.match(h.text(), /Something went wrong/, "while the failed section shows its own failure")` became `assert.match(h.text(), /BELCORT SDN BHDOwner/, "the header falls back to role-only")`. The ticket report acknowledges it only as a follow-up ("a considered trade-off, not an oversight"), not as an accepted scope change.
findings.required_fix: Either restore an explicit register-read failure surface on Firm Home (a one-line ErrorMessage where the section stood), or get the loss recorded as accepted on #995 rather than deferred to an unfiled follow-up.

findings.title: #974's row is silently withheld for any client whose register status is not 'active', which AC1 does not carve out and no cell covers
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "A client with a proposed, unsigned authority produces exactly one queue row". The installed CTE narrows that: packages/db/migrations/0260_depreciation_authority_pending_rowkind.sql:219-222 (and the live prosrc read back off clara_l07) joins `clara.clients active_fda_client on active_fda_client.id=fda.client_id and active_fda_client.status='active'`, so an onboarding, archived or otherwise-statused client with a proposed authority produces ZERO rows — precisely the client whose depreciation lane the ticket says is blocked. The migration comment defends it as house consistency ("The active-client guard mirrors eight of the other ten kinds (0017 R1-F5)"), which is a reasonable reading, but the narrowing is nowhere in the ticket and packages/db/tests/depreciation-authority-pending-rowkind.test.mjs has no cell for a non-active client, so it is an unstated, untested restriction on the AC.
findings.required_fix: Add a cell pinning the chosen behaviour for a non-active client (whichever way it is ruled), and record the narrowing in the ticket report's AC1 evidence rather than only in the migration comment.

findings.title: #1009 AC1's "its link lands on the accept control" is only ever verified to the URL, never to the control
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "- [ ] With one agreement unaccepted, an owner's Firm Home shows the prompt naming that agreement and version, and its link lands on the accept control." Both cells stop at the href/URL: apps/web/components/firm/firm-home/firm-legal-standing-tile.test.tsx:88 asserts `link.getAttribute("href") === "/settings/firm"`, and apps/web/e2e/home-board-walk.spec.ts:1280-1281 clicks the link and asserts only `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/settings\/firm$/)` — the walk never asserts that the accept control (LegalStandingCard's accept affordance, apps/web/components/firm-admin/legal-standing-card.tsx via firm-settings-panel.tsx:221) is on the page it landed on. The destination is correct in fact (I confirmed apps/web/app/(firm)/settings/firm/page.tsx mounts FirmSettingsPanel which mounts LegalStandingCard), so this is an evidence gap rather than a wrong link — but the AC's own words are about the control, not the route.
findings.required_fix: Extend the browser walk by one assertion after the navigation: the accept control is visible on /settings/firm for that owner.

findings.title: #995 AC2's client-count fallback holds only while the register read resolves, and no cell pins the below-floor caller's count when it does not
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "- [ ] A caller below the bookkeeper floor still sees a client count on Firm Home, sourced from the register read the removed tally used." apps/web/components/firm/firm-home/firm-home-board.tsx:141-144 renders `t("roleOnly")` — role, no count — whenever `register.loading || register.error`, so the fallback the ticket makes load-bearing is itself conditional. The new cell (firm-home-board.test.tsx, "a caller below the bookkeeper floor still sees a client count...") only exercises the resolved path (403 on the portfolio pack, 200 on /rest/v1/clients). summary: Four tickets, eleven commits, all four built rather than found already satisfied — correctly: I checked each ticket's premise against the branch and each was live. Spec fidelity is high and the evidence trails are unusually specific. One acceptance criterion is genuinely unmet: #974's row gets a distinct LABEL but not a distinct AFFORDANCE — it opens /clients/<id>/registers under the string 'Open the registers tab', byte-identical to the two register kinds that already exist, with a null entry in the affordance registry, and the report's cited evidence for that line (p974.row.distinct) proves something else entirely. Beyond that: #998 leaves two comments pointing at a file and a code path it deleted; #995 silently retired Firm Home's only failed-register-read surface without a ticket line asking for it; #974 narrows AC1 to active clients only, unstated and untested; #1009's link AC is verified to the URL but never to the control, and its required browser walk is not reproducible on the branch as committed (a pre-existing, out-of-lane build blocker). I re-ran every cell carrying a load-bearing claim: 60/60 on the four db files, 31/31 on activity-feed (which closes #998 AC3, left unverified by its report), 70/70 on the six web files.
